info.title: Teethi
info.description: API powering the Teethi Patient app, Doctor app, and Admin dashboard.

get.summary:
"Post-visit" (§5.1) — the patient's own read side of §6's
doctor-written recommendations

post.description:
A saved payment method (`save_payment_method: true` alongside a
fresh `token`) is always saved on the *paying* account's own
profile, not the (possibly-dependent) profile the appointment is
for — one saved card is meant to be reusable across every profile
the account manages (`PayAppointmentRequest`'s ownership check
already allows using any of them via `payment_method_id`), not
duplicated per dependent.
post.summary:
"Card/Apple Pay (stubbed) or pay-later" (§5.1). Not `LogsPhiAccess`
— invoices/payments are billing records, not one of the PHI
categories §4.12 lists (patient profiles, medical history,
clinical notes, treatment plans/tooth charts, prescriptions,
insurance, legal documents, messages)

Signs out every other device, the same token revocation
`changePassword` and `resetPassword` use, but keeping the token
that made this request so the caller isn't logged out too

post.description:
Known and unknown emails get the same `200` and message (H7), so the
endpoint can't be used to find out who has an account. A code is
only issued, and only ever exposed in dev, for a real account.
post.summary:
OTP-based, not Laravel's mail-link broker (§ decision: a 6-digit
code typed into the app matches how every other verification step
already works, and doesn't need a deep link / webview to consume
a token from)

get.summary:
Open slots for a single doctor/visit_type/date, for the booking
flow's calendar step. Not paginated — a single day's open slots
are inherently few (bounded by the doctor's own working hours),
not an arbitrary-length collection

data.description:
array_values(), not just Collection::values(): guarantees a
true 0-indexed list, which Collection::values() alone doesn't
statically prove to PHPStan through this method-chain.

get.summary:
The doctor's own open slots for one date and visit type, in the same
shape as `GET /patient/availability`. Rescheduling accepts only an
exact open slot start, so this is what the dentist app picks from
and sends back (`starts_at` as `scheduled_at`). Not paginated, for
the same reason as the patient endpoint: one day's slots are few

data.description:
array_values(), not just Collection::values(): guarantees a
true 0-indexed list, which Collection::values() alone doesn't
statically prove to PHPStan through this method-chain.

get.summary: Read-only, shared by both mobile apps for the city-selection step

Read-only (§5.3 only ever lists `GET /city-requests`, no admin
mutation of a request's own `status` — presumably it flips to
`notified` as a side effect of the requested city actually being
added via `update()` above, not a direct admin action on the
request row itself)

Every currently active patient-facing consent form template,
annotated with whether the target profile (self, or a dependent
via `?patient_profile_id=`) has already signed the exact version
shown here

consent_pending.description:
The account holder's own consent status only — a dependent's
separately-tracked signature isn't summarized here; the
consent-forms screen (§5) is where a per-profile check belongs.

post.summary:
Upserts by `token`: the same physical device can only ever belong
to one signed-in account, so re-registering it (e.g. after a
different user logs into the same device) reassigns it rather than
leaving a stale row pointing at the previous owner

patch.summary:
Unlike a patient profile, a doctor profile always has exactly one
`User` (1:1, no dependent concept) — no "nothing to toggle" case

post.summary:
Templates are never edited in place — publishing "a new version"
is always this same `store()` action, which auto-assigns the next
`version` number for the type and, when `is_active` is true (the
default), deactivates whichever version of that type was
previously live — enforcing "one active version per type" without
a separate activate endpoint. See `DocumentTemplateService::publish()`

get.description:
Not paginated: `lang/{locale}/enums.php` (see there for the exact,
current set of groups/values) is a small, fixed reference catalog —
a handful of KB at most — not a growable per-row resource list, so
decision #6's pagination rule doesn't apply here.

Calling `trans('enums')` with no specific nested key returns the
translator's entire loaded array for that file/locale unchanged
(Laravel only runs placeholder replacement when a `$replace` array
is given, which this call omits) — so this stays byte-for-byte in
sync with the lang file with no manual enum-by-enum wiring to
maintain here.
get.summary:
The full `value => localized label` catalog for every enum in the
app, keyed by the same group names as `lang/{locale}/enums.php`
(e.g. `appointment_status`, `treatment_category_group`) — read-only,
shared by all three apps, so none of them need to hand-maintain a
duplicate label map client-side. Respects `Accept-Language` the
same as every other response's `message` string

`?filter[status]=`/`?filter[patient_profile_id]=`/
`?filter[doctor_profile_id]=`, `?sort=standard_amount` (or
`-standard_amount`, `created_at`, `-created_at`) — "search/filter"
per §5.3's sketch, upgraded from a handful of `when()` clauses to
`spatie/laravel-query-builder` once Phase 9 introduced it (§6)

Addition beyond §5.3's original sketch, which only listed the
verify/reject actions — an admin needs some way to find the
documents awaiting review in the first place. `?status=submitted`
is the review queue; other statuses are still browsable for audit

patch.summary:
Marks every currently-unread notification for this account read in
one call — `unreadNotifications()` is the `Notifiable` trait's own
relation (already scoped to `read_at IS NULL`), so this is just
`markRead()` without a single target id

get.summary:
Every patient this doctor has actually engaged with — the same
status whitelist `DoctorProfile::hasTreatedPatient()` uses, applied
as a query so the "Patients" tab and the per-patient chart gate
can never disagree on who counts. `?q=` searches first/last name

Everything this doctor is allowed to see about this patient: the
profile, medical history (read-only here, §6), every appointment
between the two of them, the treatment plans/prescriptions tied to
those appointments, and this doctor's own notes about the patient.
An addition beyond §5.2's original bare sketch ("requires an
     * appointment relationship") — the shape of what it actually returns
was left to this implementation

patch.summary:
Only an account-holder profile has a `User` of its own to
(de)activate — a dependent never logs in themselves, so there's no
individual account to toggle without affecting the whole family
that manages them

get.summary:
Read-only permission catalog, for building the role-editing UI.
Gated by `permission:view_roles` at the route level — no dedicated
Policy, since there is nothing row-specific to authorize here

The "audited export" half of §6 Phase 9 — every matching row
(respecting the same filters as `index()`) in one unpaginated
response, capped well above any realistic single review window so
it stays a bounded read rather than an unbounded one

post.summary:
Uploads (or replaces) the account's avatar. Private disk only,
like every other upload in this domain (insurance cards, legal
document credentials, message attachments) — `UserResource`
resolves `profile_image` into a short-lived signed URL, never a
public path

get.summary:
`q` (name search), `city_id`, `specialization_id`, `treatment_id`,
`available_today` filter the directory. `latitude`/`longitude` (+
optional `radius_km`, default 50) switch to "near me" mode: every
other filter still applies, but results are then sorted by
distance and paginated in PHP instead of at the database — the
same trade-off `Doctor\RequestController::open()` already makes
for proximity-sorting the open pool, and for the same reason (the
matching set is never large enough for that to matter perf-wise)

Public (reviewer-name-only) review list backing the doctor detail
page's "reviews" section — see `ReviewResource` for what's
deliberately withheld

get.description:
Distance is computed in PHP (Haversine), not a raw SQL trig
expression — the open pool is never large enough for that to
matter perf-wise, and it keeps this query portable across the
app's MySQL connection and the test suite's SQLite one (which has
no acos()/radians() functions built in).
get.summary:
Unclaimed open-pool requests. `scope=nearby` (default) sorts by
distance (and, when the doctor has set `service_radius_km`, drops
requests beyond it) from the doctor's own practice address, closest first,
per the proposal's "sorted by proximity, from close to the
     * doctor's main address to further away"; requests whose visit
address has no coordinates yet sort last rather than being
excluded. `scope=all` skips distance sorting entirely (latest
request first) — e.g. for a doctor whose own practice address
isn't pinned yet

This doctor's own currently active accepted work, for the
home-screen "accepted requests" list

Direct requests addressed to this doctor that they haven't yet
accepted or declined — invisible to `open()` (unassigned pool
only) and `accepted()` (already past this decision)

Read-only catalog, shared by the doctor app (selecting expertise)
and the patient app (browsing/filtering providers)

The acting dashboard account's own roles/permissions — deliberately
not gated by any `permission:` middleware (see `StaffMeResource`),
so any `role:admin` account can call this regardless of what
dashboard permissions they hold, including holding none at all

post.summary:
A staff account is provisioned directly by another dashboard user,
not self-registered — so, unlike `AuthController::register()`,
email is marked verified immediately rather than going through the
OTP flow. forceCreate: `email_verified_at` is deliberately excluded
from `User::$fillable` (see `User::booted()`'s sibling comment on
`phone_verified_at`), so a plain `create()` would silently drop it

patch.summary:
`name`/`email`/`status` only — password changes go through the
existing `POST /forgot-password` flow (by the staff member
themselves), not this endpoint, to avoid a second surface for
setting another account's credentials. Self-deactivation via
`status` is blocked in `UpdateStaffRequest`

post.summary:
Creates the plan's chart and, when `teeth` is given, bulk-saves
every entry in it — the "bulk chart save" endpoint (§6)

put.summary:
The per-tooth upsert endpoint (§6) — creates or updates exactly
one tooth's entry

get.summary:
Read-only catalog, shared by both mobile apps' service-selection
screens. `quick_select=1` narrows to the handful of treatments
surfaced as "quick slides" (Teeth Cleaning, Teeth Whitening, ...)

post.summary:
forceCreate: `created_by` is deliberately excluded from
`Treatment::$fillable` — it must always be the acting admin's own
id, never client input, so a plain `create()` would silently drop
it (same reasoning as `PatientProfile.managing_user_id`)

forceCreate: `doctor_profile_id` is deliberately excluded from
`$fillable` — it must always be the authenticated doctor's own
profile id, never client input (same reasoning as
`PatientProfile.managing_user_id`)

Written once at the end of a visit; resubmitting overwrites the
existing row in place (`VisitOutcome`'s docblock) rather than
rejecting the second call as a conflict

treatments.description:
Every treatment actually covered by this appointment — the
single `treatment` above is just the first one selected at
booking time (kept for backward-compat display); a visit
can cover more than one procedure (§6 "book more than one
 procedure"), and this is what `InvoiceService` itself
totals up.

currency.description: Decision #9: the currency of every amount on this visit.

anyOf.description:
whenLoaded() alone isn't enough here: doctor_profile_id is
genuinely nullable (an open-pool request has no doctor
yet), and a *loaded-but-null* relation still reaches
`whenLoaded()`'s value branch — wrapping that null in
`new DoctorProfileResource(null)` would render as an
object of all-null fields, not JSON `null` (DelegatesToResource
has no null guard). Same reasoning for `insurance` below.

Same minimum-necessary masking as insurance above — a
doctor performing a visit has no clinical need to see the
patient's billing/payment status.

CancelAppointmentRequest.description:
Shared by both the patient and doctor sides of `PATCH
/appointments/{appointment}/cancel` — "cancel requires a cancellation
 * reason" per the proposal.
CancelAppointmentRequest.title: CancelAppointmentRequest

account_status.description:
Only present when the controller eager-loads `user` (the
admin directory does; nothing else currently needs it) —
a scalar field, so the loaded-but-null relation guard
other fields here need doesn't apply.

DocumentTemplateType.description: The three signable, admin-authored document types (§4.4). Credential uploads (`dental_license`, `liability_insurance`) have no template — they're a doctor-submitted file + metadata, never admin-authored text — so they live only on `LegalDocumentType`, not here.
DocumentTemplateType.title: DocumentTemplateType

file_url.description:
Never a public path — a short-lived signed URL onto the
private `local` disk, regenerated on every read rather
than stored (same pattern as InsuranceDetailResource).

attachment_url.description:
Never a public path — a short-lived signed URL onto the
private `local` disk, regenerated on every read (same
pattern as InsuranceDetailResource).

full_name.description: Decision #10: what every app displays for this patient.

account_status.description:
The *managing* account's status/email/phone, not `user`'s
— a dependent has no login of their own (`user_id` is
null), so "this patient's account" always means the
account holder who manages them. Only present when the
controller eager-loads `manager` (the admin directory
does; nothing else currently needs it).

PaymentMethodType.description: "PaymentMethodType", not "PaymentMethod" — that name is taken by the `PaymentMethod` model (a *saved* card/wallet), which this enum is itself a column on (`payments.method` and `payment_methods.provider` both describe which of these a row used).
PaymentMethodType.title: PaymentMethodType

anyOf.description:
Loaded-but-null guard (see TreatmentPlanItemResource) —
treatment_id is null for a custom-title recommendation.

currency.description: Decision #9: every amount carries its currency (E11).

role.description: Only the Patient and Doctor apps self-register; admins are provisioned separately.

RescheduleAppointmentRequest.description:
Shared by both the patient and doctor sides of `PATCH
/appointments/{appointment}/reschedule` — "Reschedule requires a
 * reschedule reason" per the proposal.
RescheduleAppointmentRequest.title: RescheduleAppointmentRequest

SignDocumentRequest.description:
Shared by both `POST /doctor/agreements` and `POST
/doctor/nondiscrimination` — a doctor never signs on behalf of anyone
else, so unlike the patient consent-form flow there's no
`patient_profile_id` here.
SignDocumentRequest.title: SignDocumentRequest

tooth_number.description:
Emergency flow's tooth selector + complaint description —
optional for every visit_type, not just "emergency"; a
routine booking may still want to flag a specific tooth.
Same 1-32 universal numbering ToothChartEntry uses.

treatment_ids.description:
A booking may cover more than one procedure in the same
visit (e.g. a cleaning + a filling) — every id is attached
to the appointment's `treatments` pivot (BookingService),
the same relation a doctor later extends mid-visit (§6).
'distinct' rejects a repeated id outright rather than
silently deduping it server-side.

StoreAvailabilityExceptionRequest.description:
`date` is a calendar date in the doctor's zone (decision #7), so "today
 * or later" is checked against the doctor's own today, not the server's
UTC date.
StoreAvailabilityExceptionRequest.title: StoreAvailabilityExceptionRequest

patient_profile_id.description:
Omit for the account holder's own profile; pass a
dependent's id to file insurance on their behalf.

attachment.description:
Images and PDFs only (Phase 10): attachments are served from
the API's own origin, so an HTML or SVG file could run script.

StorePostVisitRecommendationRequest.description:
One recommendation per call — up to 3 per appointment, enforced by
`PostVisitRecommendationService`, not here (that's a count against
existing rows, not a shape a `FormRequest` validates in isolation).
StorePostVisitRecommendationRequest.title: StorePostVisitRecommendationRequest

StoreToothChartRequest.description:
Creates the chart for a plan and, when `teeth` is given, bulk-saves
every entry in one call — the "bulk chart save" half of §6's tooth
chart checklist item (the other half, the per-tooth upsert, is
`UpsertToothChartEntryRequest`).
StoreToothChartRequest.title: StoreToothChartRequest

StoreTreatmentExpertiseRequest.description:
Either a catalog pick (`is_custom = false`, `treatment_id` required) or
an unlisted specialty/service (`is_custom = true`, `custom_title`
required) — never a mix of both. Cross-field rules live in
`withValidator()` rather than `required_if`/`prohibited_if`, since
those compare against a literal string value and `is_custom` arrives
as a real JSON boolean.
StoreTreatmentExpertiseRequest.title: StoreTreatmentExpertiseRequest

StoreTreatmentPlanRequest.description:
The plan and every one of its items are created together in one call
(`TreatmentPlanService::createWithItems()`) — there's no separate
"add an item" endpoint (see `TreatmentPlan`'s docblock).
StoreTreatmentPlanRequest.title: StoreTreatmentPlanRequest

StoreVisitOutcomeRequest.description:
Written once at the end of a visit; resubmitting overwrites the
existing row in place (`VisitOutcome`'s docblock).
StoreVisitOutcomeRequest.title: StoreVisitOutcomeRequest

anyOf.description:
whenLoaded() alone isn't enough: treatment_id is genuinely
nullable (a custom item has none), and a loaded-but-null
relation still reaches whenLoaded()'s value branch —
wrapping that null in new TreatmentResource(null) would
render as an object of all-null fields, not JSON null.

Loaded-but-null guard (see TreatmentPlanItemResource) — a
freshly created plan has no tooth chart yet.

UpdateAccountStatusRequest.description:
Shared by `PATCH /admin/patients/{patient}/status` and `PATCH
/admin/doctors/{doctor}/status` — both just flip the same underlying
`users.status`.
UpdateAccountStatusRequest.title: UpdateAccountStatusRequest

UpdateAddressRequest.description:
Shared by both the patient (home) and doctor (practice) address
endpoints — the owning profile and address `type` are set by the
controller, not the request body.
UpdateAddressRequest.title: UpdateAddressRequest

UpdateTreatmentExpertiseRequest.description:
`is_custom` and `treatment_id` are fixed at creation and never
editable here — only the expertise level, active flag, and (for a
custom entry only) its title/description may change.
UpdateTreatmentExpertiseRequest.title: UpdateTreatmentExpertiseRequest

UpdateTreatmentPlanRequest.description:
Addition beyond §5.2's original sketch (see `TreatmentPlan`'s
docblock) — the only way a plan ever leaves `draft`.
UpdateTreatmentPlanRequest.title: UpdateTreatmentPlanRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
